key_insight: FVAttn makes sparse attention for video generation faster and more scalable by balancing work across GPUs at runtime. It turns uneven adaptive Top-p routing from a bottleneck into a distributed efficiency gain.
problem_solved: Video Diffusion Transformers rely on self-attention over long spatio-temporal sequences, which is expensive for high-resolution video generation. Existing training-free sparse attention methods reduce compute, but adaptive Top-p routing creates uneven per-head workloads across GPUs, causing rank-level stragglers during sequence parallelism.
method: Introduces a training-free sparse-attention system for video generation.
Uses runtime load balancing to smooth out workload heterogeneity across attention heads and GPUs.
Improves distributed execution efficiency under multi-GPU sequence parallelism without requiring model retraining.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means faster and more reliable high-resolution video generation with lower distributed overhead. It is especially useful for scaling diffusion transformers where attention cost and GPU imbalance limit throughput.

paper_title: FVAttn: Adaptive Sparse Attention with Runtime Load Balancing for Video Generation
paper_authors: Hao Liu, Chenghuan Huang, Ye Huang, Zhiying Wen, Hao Liu
